summary: Jack Goody worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at St Albans School and St John's College (~1946–1954), and later served as a professor at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1984).

Jack Kornfield is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dartmouth under Wing-tsit Chan, earned a PhD at Saybrook, and trained under Ajahn Chah, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. He held a post at Spirit Rock Meditation Center (~1987).
Jack Laughlin works in indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999 and held an academic post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Ensink worked in indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1945–1952) and served as a lecturer and later professor at the University of Groningen from 1954.

Jacob Grimm was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1805). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and the Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

Jacob N. Kinnard works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and indology. He has held academic posts at the College of William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob Neusner was a religious studies scholar who studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Oxford, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. He held positions at UW–Milwaukee, Brandeis, University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~2000–2014).

Jacob P. Dalton specializes in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and held posts at the British Library, SOAS, Yale (2005), and UC Berkeley (attested 2011–2026).

Jacob Samuel Speyer was an indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), Groningen (1888–1903), and Leiden (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel was an indologist and linguist who studied at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig under Theodor Benfey and Friedrich Nietzsche. He held professorial chairs and posts at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and Göttingen (1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at SFSU and UCLA under William R. LaFleur, and served as professor at Princeton (1990–2019) with an affiliation at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst works in indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner and held posts at the University of Manchester (attested 2005, and as Honorary Research Fellow attested 2026).

Jacques André worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1930–1948), he held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot was a tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1919) and the University of Paris (~1936–1958), also serving as president of Société Asiatique.

Jacques Gernet was a sinologist and historian who studied at Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at CNRS, EPHE, the University of Paris, EFEO, Paris Diderot University (~1970–1973), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès specialized in sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon, and taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and École du Louvre (1998–2008), later serving as president of the Guimet Museum (2008–2011).

Jacques Leider works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne, INALCO under Denise Bernot, and Luxembourg, and held teaching posts at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2001).

Jacques May was a scholar in Buddhist studies, indology, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Constantin Régamey (~1952–1957) and served as editor-in-chief at Hōbōgirin (~1968–1981) and professor at the University of Lausanne (~1968–1992).

Jacques Scheuer was an indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau, and served as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (~1977–2007) and at Centre Sèvres.
